tagline: Limestone-bay country on the Andaman — home to James Bond Island, the Similans, and Khao Lak
introHtml:
Phang Nga is the Andaman province people picture the moment they think of Phang Nga Bay — a wide bay with hundreds of limestone karsts rising straight out of the water, including Khao Tapu, the spire everyone calls James Bond Island. You can boat out from a pier in town or take a longtail through sea caves and kayak among the mangroves all day. The town itself is small and quiet, tucked into a limestone valley with caves and cliffs flanking both sides of the road.

The north of the province has Khao Lak and Takua Pa, the launch points for dive trips to the Similan and Surin Islands, where the Andaman water is at its clearest. Out in the bay, Koh Yao Noi and Koh Yao Yai are still slow, village-style islands. People come to Phang Nga to cruise the bay among the karsts, dive the outer islands, and take the sea at an unhurried pace.
bestTime: November–April, when the sea is calm and the skies are clear — the season the Similan and Surin Islands open, and the best time for boating and diving. The rains come heavy from May to October.

highlights.name: Phang Nga Bay and Khao Tapu
highlights.blurb: A wide bay with hundreds of limestone karsts standing in the water. The most famous is Khao Tapu, better known as James Bond Island, along with the leaning Khao Phing Kan. Take a longtail out from the pier through sea caves and paddle among the mangroves all day.

highlights.name: Similan Islands
highlights.blurb: An island group out in the Andaman known for clear water and reefs, with the landmark Sail Rock and white-sand bays on Island Eight. Speedboats run from Thap Lamu pier for diving and swimming on a full-day round trip.

highlights.name: Surin Islands
highlights.blurb: An island group further out to the north, with healthy shallow-water reefs and the Moken sea-gypsy village at Ao Bon. People come to snorkel and camp on the islands — the feel is rawer and quieter than the other islands.

highlights.name: Khao Lak
highlights.blurb: A long beach in the north of the province that serves as a base for trips out to the Similans and Surins. It has quiet stretches of sand, seaside resorts, and the Tsunami Memorial built around Police Boat 813, marking the 2004 disaster.

highlights.name: Koh Yao Noi and Koh Yao Yai
highlights.blurb: Two islands in the middle of Phang Nga Bay where life still runs on rubber tapping and fishing. Quiet beaches, cycling past rice paddies under the hills — good for a long, slow stay with none of the bustle.

highlights.name: Takua Pa Old Town
highlights.blurb: A district of old Sino-Portuguese shophouses from the tin-mining era, with a historic main street and a Sunday morning market for local food and a look at the old architecture.

foodScene.name: Andaman seafood
foodScene.note: On the coast with working fishing piers, there's fresh shrimp, crab, fish, and shellfish. Seafood spots in town and along the Khao Lak shore do it steamed, grilled, stir-fried with chili (phat cha), and in tom yum.

foodScene.name: Hokkien noodles and dim sum
foodScene.note: With roots in the Hokkien Chinese community from the mining era, Phang Nga and Takua Pa have Hokkien stir-fried yellow noodles and morning dim sum shops — steamed buns, dumplings, and kopi coffee.

foodScene.name: Bold southern Thai food
foodScene.note: Gaeng tai pla, yellow curry, khua kling, and stir-fried sator with shrimp, eaten with hot rice and fresh raw vegetables on the side. These are everyday local meals you'll find all over the province.

foodScene.name: Southern khanom jeen
foodScene.note: A popular breakfast — khanom jeen rice noodles in a bold southern curry sauce, eaten with all kinds of fresh vegetables: long beans, pennywort, and young cashew leaves.

foodScene.name: Koh Yao seafood
foodScene.note: On Koh Yao Noi and Koh Yao Yai there's fish, squid, and crab straight off the village boats. The beachside spots cook it simple and home-style, with a view over Phang Nga Bay.

foodScene.name: Snacks at Takua Pa's morning market
foodScene.note: The Sunday morning market in Takua Pa Old Town has local treats — traditional sweets, fried snacks, and Chinese-southern breakfasts to graze your way through the morning.

foodScene.name: Cafes in the old town and by the sea
foodScene.note: Takua Pa Old Town and the Khao Lak area have cafes set in old buildings and laid-back seaside spots. Stop for a coffee mid-walk through town or before heading out on a boat.

attractions.name: Ao Phang Nga National Park
attractions.blurb: A wide bay full of limestone karsts in the water, with Khao Tapu, the leaning Khao Phing Kan, and sea caves to pass through. Take a longtail or kayak among the mangroves and rock islands all day.

attractions.name: Similan Islands
attractions.blurb: A clear-water island group known for its reefs and the landmark Sail Rock on Island Eight. Speedboats run from Thap Lamu for snorkeling and swimming off the white-sand beaches.

attractions.name: Surin Islands
attractions.blurb: A remote island group to the north with healthy shallow-water reefs and a Moken sea-gypsy village. Snorkel and camp on the islands, close to nature.

attractions.name: Khao Lak and the Tsunami Memorial
attractions.blurb: A long beach that serves as a base for trips out to the islands, with seaside resorts and the memorial to Police Boat 813, washed ashore by the 2004 tsunami.

attractions.name: Koh Yao Noi
attractions.blurb: An island in the middle of Phang Nga Bay where village life still holds — quiet beaches, rice paddies under the hills, and simple places to stay. Good for cycling and a long, slow stay.

attractions.name: Takua Pa Old Town
attractions.blurb: A district of Sino-Portuguese shophouses from the tin-mining era. Walk the old street, take in the architecture, and stop by the Sunday morning market for local food.

attractions.name: Wat Tham Suwan Khuha
attractions.blurb: A temple inside a limestone cave with a large reclining Buddha and stalactites and stalagmites within. It's revered by locals and a worthwhile stop on the way into town.

attractions.name: Sai Rung Waterfall and the Emerald Pool
attractions.blurb: A waterfall and clear pool in the province's forest. Walk in to swim in the cool, shaded stream — good for a day when you want to swap the sea for fresh water.
